_comment: The graphs inside cat-harness's `library` sub-graph, declared FROM WITHIN (#980) on the pattern of `sdlc/graph.json`: the `library-graph` entry of `cat-harness.json` names this directory, and this node names what it holds. Each entry is `subgraph: true` — a directory of the INSTANCE, listed by `resolveDirectories` with `within: "library-graph"`. Paths are relative to THIS directory. The skills and processes are on everywhere; the corpus alone is OPT-IN (`optIn: true` on its entry), off in every layer unless that layer lists `cat-harness.library` in its own `enableSubgraphs` (owner, 2026-11-04, card 'Library cut' option 1).
name: library

directories.description: How sources are acquired, ingested, archived, catalogued, translated and materialised, as skill packages: `library-core` and `large-datasets`. Was the `library` topic of `skills/` until 2026-11-04.

The executable library processes: content acquisition, document ingestion, translation, KG subscription and materialisation, sample import and methodology-from-source, with the DMN tables their gateways read in `decisions/`. Was the `library` concern group of `processes/` until 2026-11-04; diagrams elsewhere call them by process id.

This instance's corpus of cited sources: one `<group>/<slug>/` per ingested document, holding `sections/*.md`, `structure.json` and, where the source was scanned, `ocr/page-NNN.txt`, filed by the concern groups `library.json` names. OPT-IN (owner, 2026-11-04, card 'Library cut' option 1): off in every layer, cat-harness's own included, unless that layer lists `cat-harness.library` in its own `enableSubgraphs`, so a layer above no longer receives 85 sources (about 9,700 files) it does not cite. The id stays `library`, so a harness root resolves its corpus under the conventional id rather than the built-in default. It no longer passes the convention down: a layer above inherits `library/` from the content core, which declares `library` itself (owner, 2026-11-04, card 'Library rule' option 1, bean `wwi6`), and any layer's own `library` outranks this entry, since a declaration outranks an entry declared from within. Was `library/` until 2026-11-04. History of the entry, kept as it was written: L1 source content — one `<bib-slug>/` per ingested document, holding `sections/*.md`, `structure.json` and, where the source was scanned, `ocr/page-NNN.txt`. THIS INSTANCE HOLDS NONE. Bean `frs5` moved all four entries out (the three IRIS items to the IRIS replica, milnorlink to the science layer) because the platform holds no content, and this entry was removed with them. It is back, on the owner's ruling of 2026-09-20, for ONE reason and it is not about this instance: `wwi6` pins the guarantee that a DEPENDENT folio materialises its own `uploads/` and `library/`, and a dependent inherits the convention — an id and a relative path — from what the harness declares. Remove this and every downstream folio silently stops getting a library. IT IS THE `dh4f` SHAPE AND THAT IS KNOWN, NOT OVERLOOKED: a declared directory this instance does not hold is exactly what that bean is about. The cost is paid deliberately and it is bounded — the consumers that scan libraries now fan out over EVERY declared one (bean `a02m`), so an empty one contributes nothing rather than shadowing the two that have content. What it must never become again is the FIRST of several silently taken as the only one. The real fix is the core relocation — `uploads`, `voices`, `translation-sources` and this moving to the content core, per the owner's earlier "voices, uploads library in folio-asst-core" — after which a dependent inherits them from the layer that owns content and this entry goes for good. THE AGENT-SKILL CORPUS JOINED IT on 2026-10-01 (owner ruling: agent-skills dissolves into cat-harness's concern groups; bean `j7ql`): the 14 documents listed in `heldEntries` — vendor skill documentation (ASSERTION: a publisher describing its own product) and three arXiv papers (EVIDENCE: a measurement somebody else can repeat); each entry's `structure.json` carries its publisher, which is how a reader tells the two kinds apart. Since bean `6fez` (2026-11-01) every entry is filed by concern group at `library/<group>/<slug>/`, the groups named in `library/corpus/library.json`; the audit (#1778) put them in conduct (10), sdlc (`hmans-2026-beans-readme`), tools (`mcp-2026-specification-2026-07-28`) and content (the two RFCs). A new upload still lands unfiled at `library/<slug>/`, and ids are minted from the slug, so filing an entry changes none of them. Their summaries stay HELD, per entry, on the owner's 2026-09-24 ruling (bean `x80s`: 'Library summaries for agent-skills entries — No, keep held back'), which was stated about these documents and not about this directory.
